answer: Lineage-Divergence Claim Windows. Each identity must publish a commitment to a unique execution trace, then periodically answer a challenge derived from a ferrous hardware timestamp; a clone sharing the same trace answers identically, so any divergent response exposes the duplicate. Because clones cannot fork their history, an attacker must run genuinely separate agents with distinct traces, paying full compute and storage for every extra identity rather than copying one. A public mesa index maps trace roots to owners, and a lightweight kernel check rejects any root seen twice,
